Title: A card idea to help allies

Messages.Author: Michael Kelly
Messages.Body:
Since Allies are so easily stolen, which is the main reason
it is hard to make a deck based on them, how about the following
card.

Loyalty - Master Common
Put this card on an Ally you control. This ally cannot
be affected by (D) actions which would change who controls it.
No methuselah may play a master cards which would affect
who controls this ally.

I'd be willing to bet that with this card allies would become
more popular and effective without breaking balance.

Do others find they have trouble with stolen allies??? It's rarely
been a problem with my group. Far Mastery is such a specific interest

Muddles is cheap. Arms Dealer is free, and not unique.
I've tried to use allies a few times, and the best result was
Giovanni/Malkavian dom/nec/obf. Muddles dispatched 2 vamps before dying,
wich didn't matter coz it was out of the ash heap in no time. Fresh to
pound others again *in the same turn*. I only have one Compel the Spirit,
but Carlotta helped a bit.

> I've never found allies to be useful.
>

I probably would have won faster with a Malk stealth&bleed, but
the point was having fun. I wouldn't recommend it for an important game.

I also noticed with that deck that Malk Dementia can permanently
steal a Malkavian. You steal him on your master. You act with it. Assuming
it didn't got burned (tho it should), you can recover the Malk Dem from
your ash heap. Next turn, during your untap phase, you untap him and
return him to his owner. Master phase, guess what: Malk is mine again.
Untapped, and ready for action.
This has a number of ways to stop happening, but there's no such
thing as a flawless strategy in VtES (thank god).

David Pontes

groups of people who support this notion. Is your JOL group so large and
encompassing that it precludes this type of isolation? If that is the case,

periodically at our games, never wins, but could be used to support
Nosferatu as voters in the same way your argument seems to support Allies
as an effective strategy...

> Ghoul, and the Renegade Garou IMHO are worth the cost in pool. The built

Here your argument is very weak. Your action costs the Methuselah
controlling your target one combat card, where as that Methuselah's action
is apt to cost you four or more pool... A built in rush doesn't come close
to making up for that, especially since any decent combat deck is going to
get into combat at will anyway.

common. But that's just my two cents. If it were a dom/pre card, it
would have to be something like...hmm...what names are left from the RPG

don't know. It could go something like...take an action to place this
card on an ally. This action is at +1 stealth. An ally with this card
on it may not be affected by D actions which change the controlling
player. Blah blah blah. Obviously this text isn't perfect as it is
coming straight out of my muddled mind at nealry 3 in the morning.
Anyway, I think it preserves more of the flavor to make it
discipline-based, and I suppose it needs some provision to be
removed...but who cares right now...

It's not a bad concept, but nothing is forever. I'd probably change
the
text so that "Any Vampire burns 1 blood when attempting (D) actions
against this minion". Or make (D) actions at - stealth. If all the
cards
were untouchable, jyhad would lose a lot of it's flavor. It's important

Anyway, that's my 2 cents..

A good point! Mortals are mortal, only the dead may last forever.
In my playgroup, ally decks show up regulary. They mostly have a LOT of
intercept and really tough allies (Tremere & Gangrel mostly).
So Cards like Far Mastery are useful but often intercepted. Nearly no
deck has more than one or two, so it won't crash game balance.

Simple mortals (most Brujah Allies) are weaker than most Vamps, but they
are mere mortals. If it comes to other supernatural creatures (Garou,
Mages, Faeries, Ghosts) they naturally are more powerful and likely to
survive the harsh environment of the Jyhad. That's life.
